statement: An even landing in the cube-not-square cell n^2 ≤ x < n^3 is FiniteProgress. False. For n=3 the even x=16 lies in [9,27) and T(16)=4 ≥ 3. The second even then drops: T(4)=2 < 3. 1517 takes the odd branch (43916043). This is not PredClosure, not a Z5 family, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 and n^2 ≤ x < n^3, then an even x resets to n ≤ T(x) < n^2, and an odd x lifts to T(x) ≥ n^3. Even x < n^3 already gives T(x) < n^2 because n^3 < n^4. If that next image is also even, two even letters are FiniteProgress. On MinimalNonTerm a cube-cell even landing has odd next image. This is not a claim that a cube-cell even landing drops, not a next-letter envelope, and not a halt theorem.
